findings.source_quote: οὗ τὴν μορφὴν τὸ ἀνθρώπου βαστάζει σῶμα, οὗ εἵνεκεν ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ πάντες οἱ ἀστέρες ὑπέμειναν δουλεύειν
findings.english_quote: whose form the human body bears and for whose sake heaven and all the stars, though superior in essence, submitted to serve the one inferior in essence because of the superior one’s form.
findings.issue: The coordination makes God the antecedent of both occurrences of οὗ. That is defensible, but the second οὗ can instead refer back to the human being or human body just mentioned. This materially changes whose sake the heavenly bodies serve for. The existing note identifies the human recipient of service but does not disclose this separate antecedent ambiguity.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-quoted note explaining that the main rendering takes the successive relative clauses as referring to God, while preserving the alternative that the second means 'for the human being’s sake' or 'for the sake of the human body.' Explain that the alternative is supported by the ensuing service to the inferior recipient and the account of God’s benefits to humanity. No source correction is required.

findings.source_quote: ἵνα μηδεὶς τῶν ἀγνωμόνως ζητούντων τὸ ἀληθὲς εὕρῃ, ἀλλ’ ὃ βούλεται
findings.english_quote: so that none of those who search for the truth ungratefully may find it, but instead may find what he wants
findings.issue: The draft attaches τὸ ἀληθές to ζητούντων and supplies an understood object for εὕρῃ. This is grammatically defensible, but the more direct attachment makes 'the truth' the object of 'find,' particularly because ἀλλ’ ὃ βούλεται supplies the contrasting object of finding. The difference matters: the draft explicitly characterizes these people as searching for truth, whereas the alternative leaves their search’s object unspecified. The notes discuss gratitude terminology but not this attachment choice.
findings.suggested_revision: Prefer the source-transparent wording 'so that none of those who search ungratefully may find the truth, but instead may find what he wants.' Add a source-quoted note preserving the alternative 'those who search for the truth ... may find it' and explaining the chosen attachment through the contrasting objects of finding. Any revised wording and note require fresh review.
